questions.question: If the surface area increases for the same thrust (force), then the pressure on the surface ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **physical force** exerted on an object per unit **area**. It is mathematically expressed as **Pressure = Thrust / Area**.
 
• **Thrust** is the **total force** acting **perpendicularly** on a surface. When the **thrust** remains **constant**, the **pressure** depends solely on the **surface area** over which the force is distributed.
 
• Since **Pressure** is **inversely proportional** to the **Area** (P ∝ 1/A), any **increase** in the **surface area** will lead to a **decrease** in the **pressure** experienced by that surface.
 
• Conversely, if the **surface area** is **decreased** while the **thrust** remains the same, the **pressure** on the surface will **increase** significantly.
 
• The **SI unit** of **pressure** is the **Pascal (Pa)**, which is equivalent to **one Newton per square meter (1 N/m²)**. This unit is named after the **French scientist Blaise Pascal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Applications of Increasing Area:**
 
 
• **Foundations of buildings** are made **wide** so that the **weight** of the structure (thrust) is distributed over a **larger area**, thereby **reducing** the **pressure** on the ground and preventing the building from sinking.
 
• **School bags** are provided with **broad straps** rather than thin strings. This ensures the **weight** of the bag is spread over a **larger surface area** of the shoulder, making it **less painful** to carry by **reducing pressure**.
 
• **Tractors** and **heavy trucks** are equipped with **wide tyres** to ensure the **heavy load** does not exert enough **pressure** to sink the vehicle into soft mud or sand.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Decreasing Area:**
 
 
• A **sharp knife** has a very **small surface area** at its cutting edge. This allows a **small force** to produce a **very high pressure**, making it easy to cut through materials.
 
• **Nails** and **pins** have **pointed tips** (extremely small area) so that even a **gentle hammer strike** produces enough **pressure** to penetrate a wooden plank or a wall.
 
 
 
• **Liquid and Gas Pressure:**
 
 
• In **fluids** (liquids and gases), **pressure** is exerted in **all directions**. The **pressure** in a liquid increases with **depth** due to the weight of the overhead liquid column.
 
• **Atmospheric pressure** is the **pressure** exerted by the weight of the **atmosphere**. At **sea level**, its value is approximately **101,325 Pa** or **1 atmosphere (atm)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The relationship between **force** and **pressure** is a **fundamental principle** in **physics** and **engineering** used to design safety equipment and heavy machinery.
 
• **Scalars and Vectors:** While **force** is a **vector quantity** (having both magnitude and direction), **pressure** is a **scalar quantity** because it relates the **magnitude** of the normal force to the area.
 
• **Dimensions:** The **dimensional formula** for **pressure** is **[ML⁻¹T⁻²]**.
 
• The concept of **thrust** and **pressure** explains why a person can **walk on snow** more easily using **skis** (large area, low pressure) than wearing **normal shoes** (small area, high pressure).

questions.question: What is the key realization that can lead to more sustainable use of natural resources?

options.text: Selfish exploitation causes environmental harm and misery
Only future generations must benefit from resources

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Selfish exploitation causes environmental harm and misery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The core realization for **sustainable resource management** is that **unregulated selfish exploitation** of **natural resources** inevitably leads to **ecological degradation** and human suffering. This is often described in **environmental economics** as the **Tragedy of the Commons**.
 
• When individuals or entities prioritize **short-term profits** over **long-term stability**, they deplete **renewable resources** (like **forests** and **fisheries**) and **non-renewable resources** (like **minerals** and **fossil fuels**) beyond their **carrying capacity**.
 
• This exploitation results in **environmental harm**, such as **biodiversity loss**, **soil erosion**, and **climate change**, which directly causes **socio-economic misery** by destroying livelihoods and reducing the **quality of life** for present and future populations.
 
• Recognizing the **interconnectedness** of **ecosystems** helps society understand that **sustainable use** is not just an **ethical choice** but a **biological necessity** for survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development:** This concept was famously defined in the **Brundtland Report** (also known as **Our Common Future**) in **1987** as development that meets the needs of the **present** without compromising the ability of **future generations** to meet their own needs.
 
• **The Three Pillars:** Sustainability is built on **three interconnected pillars**: **Environmental Protection**, **Social Equity**, and **Economic Viability**. Focusing solely on **unlimited growth** (Option 2) ignores the **biophysical limits** of **Earth**.
 
• **Intergenerational Equity:** This **legal** and **ethical principle** suggests that **natural resources** belong to all generations. While **future generations** must benefit (Option 3), the realization must also encompass the **current generation's** responsible consumption to avoid **immediate misery**.
 
• **The Role of Regulation:** While **rules and legislation** are essential for **conservation** (Option 4), they are often insufficient without a **collective realization** and **cultural shift** toward **stewardship** and **voluntary compliance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Resource Depletion Data:** According to the **Global Footprint Network**, humanity is currently using **nature** **1.75 times faster** than our planet’s **ecosystems** can regenerate, leading to **ecological overshoot**.
 
• **United Nations SDGs:** The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically **Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** and **Goal 15 (Life on Land)**, were adopted in **2015** to provide a global **blueprint** for mitigating **selfish exploitation**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The **Dasgupta Review (2021)** on the **Economics of Biodiversity** highlighted that our **global economy** is embedded within **nature**, not external to it, meaning **environmental harm** eventually results in **economic collapse**.

questions.question: If a body’s velocity changes from +20 m/s to –10 m/s in 4 seconds, the acceleration is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**– 7.5 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** of an object with respect to **time**. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• The mathematical formula to calculate **average acceleration (a)** is given by: **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** is the **final velocity**, **u** is the **initial velocity**, and **t** is the **time interval**.
 
• In the given problem, the **initial velocity (u)** is **+20 m/s**, the **final velocity (v)** is **-10 m/s**, and the **time taken (t)** is **4 seconds**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **a = (-10 m/s - 20 m/s) / 4 s**. This simplifies to **a = -30 / 4**, which equals **-7.5 m/s²**.
 
• The **negative sign** indicates that the **acceleration** is acting in the **opposite direction** to the initial motion, or that the body is experiencing **retardation** relative to the positive direction. ***Hence, the correct answer is – 7.5 m/s².***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Unit of Acceleration**: The standard unit for measuring **acceleration** in the **International System of Units (SI)** is the **meter per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• **Vector Nature**: Since **velocity** is a vector, any change in either the **speed** or the **direction** of motion results in **acceleration**. In this case, the body not only slowed down but also **reversed its direction** (moving from positive to negative velocity).
 
• **Uniform vs. Non-Uniform Acceleration**: **Uniform acceleration** occurs when the **velocity** changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of **time**. **Non-uniform acceleration** occurs when the rate of change of **velocity** varies over time.
 
• **Retardation/Deceleration**: When the **acceleration** of a body is in the direction opposite to its **velocity**, it is often referred to as **deceleration** or **retardation**. It results in a decrease in the **magnitude** of velocity (speed) until the object stops or reverses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention**: In physics, **direction** is often indicated by **positive (+)** and **negative (-)** signs. A change from **+20 m/s** to **-10 m/s** implies a total change in **velocity** of **30 m/s** in the negative direction.
 
• **Instantaneous vs. Average**: While the formula **(v-u)/t** provides the **average acceleration** over the **4-second** interval, **instantaneous acceleration** refers to the acceleration at a specific **moment in time**, calculated using **derivatives (dv/dt)**.
 
• **Graphical Representation**: On a **velocity-time graph**, the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration**. A downward-sloping line indicates **negative acceleration**.

questions.question: A sample of brass is melted and poured into a mold to make a musical instrument. Which of the following correctly explains why brass is classified as a homogeneous mixture?

options.text: The components of brass are uniformly distributed and cannot be distinguished visually
The components of brass are chemically bonded and cannot be separated
Brass is made of only one type of atom and hence appears uniform
Brass is an example of a compound formed by the reaction of zinc and copper

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The components of brass are uniformly distributed and cannot be distinguished visually**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brass** is categorized as a **homogeneous mixture** because it is a **solid solution** where the **solute (zinc)** and **solvent (copper)** are mixed uniformly at the **atomic level**.
 
• In a **homogeneous mixture**, the composition is consistent throughout the entire sample, and there are no **visible boundaries** of separation between the constituent elements. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Unlike **chemical compounds**, the elements in an **alloy** are not **chemically bonded** in fixed proportions. They are physically blended in a molten state and retain their individual chemical identities. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Brass** is an **alloy**, which by definition is a mixture of two or more **elements** (at least one being a metal). It consists of **copper** and **zinc** atoms, rather than being made of a single type of atom. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more elements **chemically react** to form a new substance with entirely different properties. Brass is a **physical mixture** of metals that exhibits **variable composition**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **uniformity** of brass ensures that any small sample taken from the musical instrument will have the same **ratio of copper to zinc** as any other sample from the same mold.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Brass:** It typically consists of approximately **60% to 70% Copper (Cu)** and **30% to 40% Zinc (Zn)**. The exact **percentage** can be adjusted to alter the **hardness**, **color**, and **ductility** of the metal.
 
• **Properties:** Brass is highly prized for its **malleability** (easier to shape than bronze or zinc) and its **acoustic properties**, which make it ideal for **musical instruments** like trumpets, horns, and bells.
 
• **Corrosion Resistance:** Due to the presence of **Copper**, brass is highly resistant to **corrosion**, making it useful for **plumbing fixtures**, **marine hardware**, and **electrical terminals**.
 
• **Substitutional Alloy:** Brass is specifically a **substitutional alloy**, meaning the **Zinc** atoms replace **Copper** atoms within the **metallic crystal lattice**.
 
• **Applications:** Beyond music, it is used in **ammunition casings**, **decorative items**, and **low-friction applications** like locks, gears, and bearings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alloys vs. Mixtures:** Alloys are considered **mixtures** because they show the properties of their constituents and can have **variable compositions** (unlike compounds which have a **fixed formula**).
 
• **Separation:** While **homogeneous mixtures** cannot be separated by simple physical methods like **filtration**, the components of brass can be separated using **metallurgical processes** that exploit different **melting points** or **chemical reactivities**.
 
• **History:** Brass has been known to humans since **ancient times** (roughly **500 BC**), though it was often produced by smelting copper ores rich in zinc before pure zinc was identified as an **element**.
 
• **Identification:** To the naked eye or under a standard microscope, a **homogeneous mixture** like brass appears as a single **pure substance**, which is a key characteristic of **solid solutions**.
</ul

questions.question: In electrolytic refining, the pure metal is used as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a cathode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the process of **electrolytic refining**, the **pure metal** always serves as the **cathode**, which is the **negative electrode** in the electrolytic cell.
 
• A thin strip or rod of **pure metal** is placed at the **cathode** to act as a starter sheet upon which the refined metal will deposit.
 
• The **impure metal** (the metal to be refined) is made the **anode**, which is the **positive electrode**.
 
• When an **electric current** is passed through the circuit, the metal atoms from the **impure anode** lose electrons and enter the **electrolyte** as **positive ions**.
 
• These **positive metal ions** are then attracted to the **negative cathode**, where they gain electrons (undergo **reduction**) and deposit as **pure metal** atoms.
 
• The concentration of the **electrolyte** remains constant throughout the process because the rate at which metal dissolves from the **anode** is equal to the rate at which it deposits on the **cathode**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Electrolyte:**
 
 
• The **electrolyte** used in this process is a **soluble salt solution** of the same metal that is being refined.
 
• For example, in the **electrolytic refining of copper**, the **electrolyte** is usually a solution of **acidified copper sulphate** (CuSO4).
 
 
 
• **Commonly Refined Metals:**
 
 
• This method is widely utilized for the purification of various non-ferrous metals such as **Copper (Cu)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Tin (Sn)**, **Nickel (Ni)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**.
 
• It is particularly effective for obtaining metals with a very **high degree of purity**, often exceeding **99.9%**.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism at Electrodes:**
 
 
• At the **Anode**: The reaction involves **oxidation**, where the metal M becomes M(n+) + ne(-).
 
• At the **Cathode**: The reaction involves **reduction**, where the metal ions M(n+) + ne(-) become the pure metal M.
 
 
 
• **Treatment of Impurities:**
 
 
• Soluble impurities go into the **electrolyte solution** and remain there.
 
• Insoluble impurities, which do not dissolve, fall to the bottom of the tank just below the **anode**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Anode Mud:** This refers to the collection of **insoluble impurities** that settle under the **anode**. In many cases, **anode mud** contains valuable elements such as **antimony**, **selenium**, **tellurium**, **silver**, **gold**, and **platinum**. The recovery of these precious metals often covers the cost of the **refining process**.
 
• **Copper Refining:** In the specific case of **copper**, the impure **anode** is often referred to as **blister copper**. As the process proceeds, the **anode** gradually gets thinner while the **cathode** becomes thicker and heavier with **pure copper**.
 
• **Voltage and Current:** The process requires a carefully controlled **Direct Current (DC)** and a specific **voltage** to ensure that only the desired metal ions are reduced at the **cathode**, preventing the deposition of unwanted impurities.
</ul

questions.question: Soap molecules arrange themselves in which form to perform cleaning action?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micelles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Soap molecules are **sodium** or **potassium** salts of long-chain **carboxylic acids** (fatty acids). They possess a unique structure consisting of a **hydrophilic** (water-loving) ionic head and a **hydrophobic** (water-fearing) hydrocarbon tail.
 
• When soap is dissolved in water, the molecules orient themselves in a specific cluster called a **Micelle**. In this arrangement, the **hydrophobic** tails aggregate together at the interior of the cluster to stay away from water, while the **ionic heads** face outward, interacting with the water molecules.
 
• The cleaning action occurs because most dirt and stains are **oily** or **greasy** in nature. The **hydrophobic** end of the soap molecule attaches itself to the oil or dirt particle, while the **hydrophilic** end remains attached to the water.
 
• This results in the formation of an **emulsion** where the oily dirt is trapped at the center of the **micelle**. Since the surfaces of these **micelles** are similarly charged (usually negative), they repel each other and remain suspended in the water as a **colloid**, preventing the dirt from re-depositing on the clothes. ***Hence, the correct answer is Micelles.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Composition of Soap:**
 
 
• Common soaps are made from fats and oils reacting with **Sodium Hydroxide** (NaOH) or **Potassium Hydroxide** (KOH). This chemical reaction is known as **Saponification**.
 
• Common fatty acids used include **stearic acid**, **palmitic acid**, and **oleic acid**. **Sodium stearate** (**C17H35COONa**) is a typical example of a soap molecule.
 
 
 
• **Hard Water and Scum Formation:**
 
 
• In **hard water**, which contains high concentrations of **Calcium** (Ca2+) and **Magnesium** (Mg2+) ions, soap reacts with these ions to form an insoluble, greyish-white **precipitate** called **scum**.
 
• Because of this **precipitation**, a large amount of soap is wasted before it can start forming **micelles** for cleaning.
 
 
 
• **Detergents vs. Soap:**
 
 
• **Detergents** are generally **ammonium** or **sulphonate** salts of long-chain carboxylic acids.
 
• Unlike soaps, the charged ends of **detergents** do not form insoluble **precipitates** with the **calcium** and **magnesium** ions in hard water. Therefore, detergents are effective for cleaning even in hard water conditions.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Action:**
 
 
• The cleansing process involves **agitation** (scrubbing or rotating in a washing machine), which helps pull the **micelles** (containing the trapped dirt) away from the surface of the fabric into the bulk of the water.
 
• Soap lowers the **surface tension** of water, allowing it to wet surfaces more effectively and penetrate deeper into the fibers of the cloth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydrophobic Effect:** This is the primary driving force behind **micelle** formation. The non-polar **hydrocarbon tails** are "pushed" together by water molecules that prefer to bond with each other and the **polar heads** of the soap.
 
• **Tyndall Effect:** Because a soap solution containing **micelles** is a **colloidal** system, it is capable of scattering a beam of light, a phenomenon known as the **Tyndall effect**.
 
• **Shape:** While often represented as spheres, **micelles** can take various shapes depending on the concentration of soap and the temperature, including **ellipsoidal** or **cylindrical** forms.
 
• **Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC):** This is the specific **concentration** of surfactants above which **micelles** form and all additional surfactants added to the system go to **micelles**. Below this concentration, soap molecules exist individually on the surface or in the bulk of the liquid.
</ul

questions.question: The magnification of a concave mirror is −1. Which of the following statements is correct about the position of the object?

options.text: Object is beyond the centre of curvature
Object is between focus and pole
Object is at the centre of curvature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Object is at the centre of curvature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **magnification (m)** of a spherical mirror is defined as the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**. It is also expressed in terms of **object distance (u)** and **image distance (v)** as **m = -v/u**.
 
• In this question, the **magnification is -1**. The **negative sign** indicates that the image formed is **real and inverted**. ***Hence, the image is formed in front of the mirror.***
 
• The **numerical value 1** indicates that the **size of the image is exactly equal to the size of the object** (|v| = |u|).
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the image is of the **same size** as the object only when the object is placed at the **centre of curvature (C)**. __
 
• **Isobars** are defined as atoms of different **chemical elements** that have the same **mass number** (total number of **nucleons**) but different **atomic numbers** (number of **protons**).
 
• The term **isobar** was suggested by **Alfred Walter Stewart** in the year **1918**. It is derived from the Greek words "isos" meaning equal and "baros" meaning weight.
 
• Because **isobars** have different **atomic numbers**, they occupy different positions in the **periodic table** and possess different **chemical properties**.
 
• Examples of **isobars** include **Argon** (**atomic number 18**), **Potassium** (**atomic number 19**), and **Calcium** (**atomic number 20**), all of which can have a **mass number** of **40**.
 
• Since their **mass numbers** are the same, their **physical properties**, which depend on the mass of the atom, may be quite similar, though their **electronic configurations** differ significantly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**
 
 
• It represents the number of **protons** found in the **nucleus** of every atom of that element.
 
• It uniquely identifies a **chemical element**. For instance, any atom with **6 protons** is an atom of **Carbon**.
 
 
 
• **Mass Number (A):**
 
 
• It is the sum of the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** in an atomic nucleus.
 
• While the **atomic number** is usually constant for an element, the **mass number** can vary, leading to the formation of **isotopes**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are atoms of the **same element** that have the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers**.
 
• Example: **Hydrogen** has three isotopes: **Protium** (1 proton, 0 neutrons), **Deuterium** (1 proton, 1 neutron), and **Tritium** (1 proton, 2 neutrons).
 
 
 
• **Isotones:**
 
 
• These are atoms of different elements that have the same number of **neutrons** but different **atomic numbers** and **mass numbers**.
 
• Example: **Carbon-14** (6 protons, 8 neutrons) and **Oxygen-16** (8 protons, 8 neutrons) are **isotones**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nucleons** is the collective term used for **protons** and **neutrons**, both of which reside in the **nucleus** of an atom.
 
• The number of **electrons** in a neutral atom is equal to its **atomic number**. Since **isobars** have different **atomic numbers**, they have a different number of **electrons**, leading to their distinct **chemical reactivity**.
 
• In nuclear physics, **isobars** are relevant in **beta decay**. In **beta minus decay**, a **neutron** turns into a **proton**, meaning the **atomic number** increases by 1 while the **mass number** remains constant, effectively creating an **isobar** of the parent atom.
 
• The **atomic mass** of an element is the weighted average of the masses of its naturally occurring **isotopes** and is measured in **atomic mass units (amu)**.

questions.question: The power of a lens is given as the reciprocal of its:

__
 
• The **power of a lens** is defined as the ability of the lens to converge or diverge light rays falling on it. It is mathematically expressed as the **reciprocal of its focal length**.
 
• The standard formula used to calculate the power (**P**) is **P = 1/f**, where **f** must be measured in **metres**.
 
• The **SI unit** of power of a lens is the **Dioptre**, which is denoted by the symbol **D**. One Dioptre is equal to **1 m⁻¹**.
 
• A **convex lens** has a **positive focal length**, and therefore, its power is always **positive**. This is because it converges light rays at a real focus.
 
• A **concave lens** has a **negative focal length**, resulting in a **negative power** value. This lens is known for diverging light rays.
 
• The power of a lens is directly related to its **refractive index** and the **radii of curvature** of its surfaces, as described by the lens maker's formula.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Focal Length and Power Relationship**: A lens with a **short focal length** has more power because it bends light rays more sharply, leading to a higher degree of **convergence** or **divergence**. Conversely, a lens with a **long focal length** has **less power**.
 
• **Optical Instruments**: Opticians prescribe corrective lenses using power instead of focal length. For example, a prescription of **+2.0 D** indicates a **convex lens** with a focal length of **0.5 metres** (50 cm).
 
• **Refractive Index Influence**: The power of a lens also depends on the medium in which it is placed. If a lens is immersed in a liquid with a **higher refractive index** than air, its **focal length increases**, and its **power decreases**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Hypermetropia (Long-sightedness)**: This condition is corrected using a **convex lens** with **positive power**, which increases the converging power of the eye's optical system.
 
• **Calculation Tip**: Always remember to convert the focal length from **centimetres** to **metres** before using the power formula. For instance, if **f = 25 cm**, then **f = 0.25 m**, and **P = 1/0.25 = 4 D**.
 
• **Physical Dimensions**: While **thickness** and **diameter** (aperture) affect the intensity of light and aberrations, they do not directly define the numerical "power" of the lens in the same way the **focal length** does.

questions.question: In a reflex arc, which of the following represents the correct path of the impulse?

options.text: Receptor → Spinal cord → Motor neuron → Muscle
Receptor → Motor neuron → Spinal cord → Muscle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Receptor → Spinal cord → Motor neuron → Muscle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **reflex arc** is a neural pathway that controls a **reflex action**, which is an immediate, **involuntary** response to a **stimulus**.
 
• The process begins at the **Receptor** (like the skin or eyes), which perceives the **stimulus** (such as heat or pain).
 
• From the receptor, the impulse is carried by a **sensory neuron** (also known as an **afferent neuron**) to the **Central Nervous System (CNS)**, specifically the **Spinal cord**.
 
• In the **Spinal cord**, the **interneuron** processes the signal and immediately relays it to a **Motor neuron** (also known as an **efferent neuron**) without waiting for the **brain** to provide a conscious command.
 
• The **Motor neuron** then transmits the impulse to the **Effector**, which is usually a **Muscle** or a gland, to perform the necessary action.
 
• The sequence **Receptor → Spinal cord → Motor neuron → Muscle** correctly identifies the bypass of the **brain** to ensure speed. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The sequence **Receptor → Spinal cord → Brain → Muscle** implies that the brain must process the reflex before the muscle acts, which would be too slow for a reflex. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The sequence **Receptor → Brain → Spinal cord → Muscle** describes a conscious voluntary action rather than an involuntary reflex. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The sequence **Receptor → Motor neuron → Spinal cord → Muscle** is anatomically incorrect because **motor neurons** carry impulses away from the **spinal cord**, not toward it. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sensory Neurons (Afferent):** These specialized **nerve cells** are responsible for converting external stimuli from the environment into internal electrical impulses. They carry signals from the **peripheral nervous system** to the **CNS**.
 
• **Motor Neurons (Efferent):** These are **neurons** located in the **CNS** that project their **axons** outside the **CNS** to directly or indirectly control **muscles** and **glands**.
 
• **Reflex Action:** This is a rapid, automatic response to a stimulus. Examples include the **knee-jerk reflex**, blinking when an object approaches the eye, or withdrawing a hand from a **hot surface**.
 
• **Evolutionary Advantage:** The primary **function** of the **reflex arc** is survival. By bypassing the **conscious brain**, the body can react to **dangerous stimuli** in milliseconds, significantly reducing the risk of **tissue damage**.
 
• **Interneurons:** These are found within the **Spinal cord** and act as the "middleman," connecting **sensory** and **motor neurons** to allow for a quick circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Reflexes:**
 
 
• **Monosynaptic Reflex:** A simple reflex arc consisting of only one **synapse** between the **sensory** and **motor neuron** (e.g., the **Patellar reflex**).
 
• **Polysynaptic Reflex:** A reflex involving one or more **interneurons** between the sensory and motor components (e.g., the **withdrawal reflex** from pain).
 
 
 
• **Anatomy of the Spinal Cord:** The **grey matter** of the spinal cord is where the **synapses** of the reflex arc occur. It contains the cell bodies of **motor neurons** and **interneurons**.
 
• **Synapse:** This is the microscopic gap between two **neurons** where the electrical impulse is converted into a **chemical signal** (using **neurotransmitters**) to cross to the next cell.
 
• **Stimulus:** Any change in the environment (internal or external) that is capable of eliciting a **nerve impulse**.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Butane (C4H10)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Butane (C4H10)** is an **alkane** with **four carbon atoms**. It is the first hydrocarbon in the series that can form a **branched chain structure** known as **isobutane** (or **2-methylpropane**), where one carbon atom is attached to the center carbon of a three-carbon chain. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• **Ethane (C2H6)** consists of **two carbon atoms** connected by a single bond. Because it only has two carbons, they can only be arranged in a **straight line**, making branching impossible. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cyclohexane (C6H12)** is a **cycloalkane** where **six carbon atoms** are joined in a **closed-ring structure**. While it contains multiple carbons, its primary arrangement is **cyclic** rather than a branched open chain. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Methane (CH4)** is the simplest **hydrocarbon**, containing only **one carbon atom** bonded to four hydrogen atoms. Since there is only one carbon, there is no possibility of any **chain formation** or branching. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In organic chemistry, **branching** occurs when at least one carbon atom is bonded to **three or four** other carbon atoms, a phenomenon that requires a minimum of **four carbon atoms** in an open-chain alkane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structural Isomerism:**
 
 
• This is a form of **isomerism** where compounds have the same **molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements** of atoms.
 
• **Butane** has two structural isomers: **n-Butane** (straight chain) and **isobutane** (branched chain).
 
• As the number of **carbon atoms** increases, the number of possible **isomers** increases significantly. For example, **Pentane (C5H12)** has **three** isomers, while **Hexane (C6H14)** has **five**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrocarbon Classification:**
 
 
• **Alkanes:** Saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula **CnH2n+2**. They contain only **single covalent bonds**.
 
• **Alkenes and Alkynes:** Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing **double** or **triple bonds**, respectively.
 
• **Cycloalkanes:** Saturated hydrocarbons where the carbon atoms are arranged in a **ring**, following the formula **CnH2n**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties of Branched Chains:**
 
 
• **Branching** generally lowers the **boiling point** of a compound compared to its straight-chain isomer.
 
• This is because a **branched-chain** molecule has a more **spherical shape**, which reduces the **surface area** and weakens the **Van der Waals forces** between molecules.
 
• For instance, **n-butane** has a boiling point of approximately **-0.5 degrees Celsius**, while **isobutane** boils at **-11.7 degrees Celsius**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carbon's Tetravalency:** Carbon has **four valence electrons**, allowing it to form **four covalent bonds**. This property, known as **tetravalency**, combined with **catenation** (the ability to link with other carbon atoms), allows the formation of complex **straight, branched, and cyclic** structures.
 
• **Nomenclature:** According to **IUPAC** rules, the branched isomer of butane is named **2-methylpropane** because the longest continuous chain has **three carbons** (propane) and a **methyl group** is attached to the **second carbon**.
 
• **Natural Occurrence:** **Butane** is a highly flammable, colorless gas that is easily **liquefied**. It is commonly used as a fuel in **LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas)** cylinders and **cigarette lighters**.
</ul

questions.question: A single-turn coil of radius R produces a magnetic field B at its centre. If the same wire is wound into a coil of n turns (each of radius R/n) carrying the same current I, what will be the value of the new field at the centre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**n²B**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **magnetic field (B)** at the center of a circular coil carrying a **current (I)** is directly proportional to the **number of turns (N)** and inversely proportional to the **radius (R)** of the coil.
 
• The mathematical formula for the magnetic field at the center of a circular loop is **B = (mu_0 * N * I) / (2 * R)**, where **mu_0** is the **permeability of free space**.
 
• In the initial case, for a **single-turn coil** (N = 1) with **radius R**, the field is **B = (mu_0 * I) / (2 * R)**. ***Hence, this represents the baseline magnetic field strength.***
 
• In the second case, the **same wire** is wound into a coil of **n turns**. This means the new number of turns **N' = n**.
 
• The new **radius (R')** is given as **R/n**. This is because the total length of the wire remains constant, so increasing the turns must reduce the radius proportionally. ***Hence, the change in radius is a direct consequence of the change in turns.***
 
• The new magnetic field **B'** is calculated as: **B' = (mu_0 * n * I) / (2 * (R/n))**. Simplifying this expression gives **B' = n² * [(mu_0 * I) / (2 * R)]**.
 
• Comparing the two equations, we find that **B' = n² * B**. ***Hence, the correct answer is n²B.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnetic Field Induction**: This phenomenon is a part of **electromagnetism**, specifically explained by the **Biot-Savart Law**, which relates magnetic fields to the magnitude, direction, length, and proximity of the electric current.
 
• **Dependence on Current**: If the **current (I)** were doubled while keeping the turns and radius constant, the **magnetic field** would also double, showing a **linear relationship**.
 
• **Permeability (mu_0)**: The constant **mu_0** has a standard value of **4 * pi * 10^-7 T*m/A**. It represents how easily **magnetic flux** can be established in a vacuum.
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**: This rule is used to determine the **direction** of the magnetic field. If the fingers of the right hand curl in the direction of the **current** in the loop, the thumb points in the direction of the **magnetic field** at the center.
 
• **Applications**: The principle of increasing **turns** to strengthen a magnetic field is widely used in **transformers**, **electric motors**, **generators**, and **electromagnets** found in industrial machinery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Length of Wire Constraint**: In such problems, it is crucial to remember that the **length of the wire (L)** is **L = 2 * pi * R * N**. If **N** is multiplied by **n**, **R** must be divided by **n** to keep **L** constant.
 
• **Squared Relationship**: The field strength at the center increases with the **square of the number of turns** (n²) when the **same length of wire** is used because both the increase in turns and the decrease in radius contribute equally to the field enhancement.
 
• **Units**: The **SI unit** for the magnetic field is the **Tesla (T)**, named after **Nikola Tesla**. Another commonly used unit is the **Gauss (G)**, where **1 Tesla = 10,000 Gauss**.
 
• **Center vs. Axis**: The formula used here is specifically for the **center** of the coil. The field at a distance **x** along the **axis** of the coil would follow a different formula involving **(R² + x²)³/2** in the denominator.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following equations does NOT correctly represent the relationship between physical quantities for an object moving with uniform acceleration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2as = v2 + u2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The equations of motion describe the basic concepts of a moving object, such as its **velocity**, **displacement**, and **acceleration**, relative to **time**. These are specifically valid for motion with **uniform acceleration** (constant acceleration).
 
• The equation **v = u + at** is known as the **first equation of motion**. It shows the relationship between **final velocity (v)**, **initial velocity (u)**, **acceleration (a)**, and **time (t)**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The equation **s = ut + 1/2at2** is the **second equation of motion**. It is used to calculate the **displacement (s)** of an object over a period of **time** when the **initial velocity** and **acceleration** are constant. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The equation **v2 - u2 = 2as** is the **third equation of motion**. It relates **final velocity**, **initial velocity**, **acceleration**, and **displacement** without involving the variable of **time**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The expression **2as = v2 + u2** does not correctly represent a standard kinematic relationship. In the correct formula, the **initial velocity squared (u2)** must be subtracted from the **final velocity squared (v2)** to equal **2as**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• These equations were famously summarized in **Sir Isaac Newton's** work, **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica**, published in **1687**, which laid the foundation for **classical mechanics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definitions of Variables:**
 
 
• **Initial Velocity (u)**: The **velocity** of the object at **time t = 0**. It is measured in **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• **Final Velocity (v)**: The **velocity** of the object after **time t** has elapsed, measured in **m/s**.
 
• **Acceleration (a)**: The rate of change of **velocity**. For these equations to hold true, **a** must be **constant**. It is measured in **meters per second squared (m/s2)**.
 
• **Displacement (s)**: The shortest distance between the starting and ending points, a **vector quantity** measured in **meters (m)**.
 
 
 
• **Graphical Representation:**
 
 
• In a **Velocity-Time (v-t) graph**, the **slope** represents the **acceleration** of the object.
 
• The **area under the curve** of a **Velocity-Time graph** represents the total **displacement** covered by the object.
 
• A **straight line** in a **v-t graph** indicates **uniform acceleration**, whereas a **horizontal line** indicates **zero acceleration** (constant velocity).
 
 
 
• **Motion Under Gravity:**
 
 
• A common application of these equations is **free fall**. In this case, **acceleration (a)** is replaced by **acceleration due to gravity (g)**, which is approximately **9.8 m/s2** on **Earth**.
 
• When an object is thrown **upward**, the value of **g** is taken as **negative** because it acts in the opposite direction of motion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conditions for Validity:** These equations are **only applicable** when the object moves in a **straight line** and the **acceleration** remains **uniform**. They cannot be used for **circular motion** or **variable acceleration** without calculus.
 
• **Retardation/Deceleration:** If the **final velocity** is less than the **initial velocity**, the **acceleration** is **negative**, often referred to as **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
• **Special Cases:**
 
 
• If an object starts from **rest**, the **initial velocity (u)** is taken as **0**.
 
• If an object comes to a **stop** (brakes applied), the **final velocity (v)** is taken as **0**.
 
 
 
• **Vector Nature:** Since **displacement**, **velocity**, and **acceleration** are **vectors**, their **direction** (positive or negative) must be consistently maintained throughout the calculation.

questions.question: The resistance of a conductor depends on the:

options.text: Length, area of cross-section, material of the conductor, and temperature
Length and area of cross-section only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Length, area of cross-section, material of the conductor, and temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **resistance** of a conductor is a property that opposes the flow of electric current through it. It is mathematically expressed by the formula **R = ρ(L/A)**, where **ρ** is the resistivity, **L** is the length, and **A** is the area of cross-section.
 
• **Length (L)**: The resistance of a conductor is **directly proportional** to its **length**. This means if the length of the wire is doubled, the resistance also doubles because electrons have to travel a longer distance and face more collisions. ***Hence, the statement regarding length is correct.***
 
• **Area of Cross-section (A)**: Resistance is **inversely proportional** to the **area of cross-section** of the conductor. A thicker wire (larger area) provides a wider path for electrons, resulting in lower resistance, whereas a thinner wire has higher resistance. ***Hence, the statement regarding the area of cross-section is correct.***
 
• **Material of the Conductor**: Resistance depends on the **nature of the material** used. Different materials have different **resistivities (ρ)** due to their unique atomic structures. For example, **Silver** and **Copper** have very low resistivity and are excellent conductors, while **Nichrome** has high resistivity. ***Hence, the statement regarding the material is correct.***
 
• **Temperature**: For **metallic conductors**, the resistance **increases with an increase in temperature**. As temperature rises, the metal ions vibrate more vigorously, increasing the frequency of collisions between flowing electrons and the ions. ***Hence, the statement regarding temperature is correct.***
 
• While **Ohm's Law** states **V = IR**, the resistance itself does not depend on the **voltage applied** or the **current flowing** through it; these are external circuit variables. Resistance is an **intrinsic physical property** of the conductor. ***Hence, the correct answer is Length, area of cross-section, material of the conductor, and temperature.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Resistivity (ρ)**: This is also known as **specific resistance**. It is the resistance offered by a conductor of **unit length** and **unit area of cross-section**. The **SI unit** of resistivity is the **Ohm-meter (Ωm)**.
 
• **Conductors vs. Insulators**: Materials with very low resistivity are called **conductors** (like **Aluminum** and **Gold**), while those with very high resistivity are **insulators** (like **Glass** and **Rubber**).
 
• **Temperature Coefficient**: Metals generally have a **positive temperature coefficient** of resistance, meaning resistance increases with heat. Conversely, **semiconductors** like **Silicon** and **Germanium** have a **negative temperature coefficient**, where resistance decreases as temperature increases.
 
• **Superconductivity**: This is a phenomenon where certain materials exhibit **zero electrical resistance** when cooled below a specific **critical temperature**. This was first discovered by **Heike Kamerlingh Onnes** in **1911**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SI Unit**: The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm**, symbolized by the Greek letter **Ω (Omega)**. It is named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm**.
 
• **Conductance**: The reciprocal of resistance is known as **conductance (G)**. Its **SI unit** is **Siemens (S)** or **mho**. A material with high resistance has low conductance.
 
• **Ohmic and Non-Ohmic Conductors**: Conductors that obey **Ohm's Law** (where V is proportional to I) are called **Ohmic conductors** (like most metals). Those that do not, such as **diodes** or **transistors**, are called **non-Ohmic**.
 
• **Effect of Stretching**: If a wire is **stretched** to double its length, its area of cross-section decreases proportionally (since volume remains constant), causing the resistance to increase by **four times** (n squared).

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by both 2 and 5?

⇒ For 134: The unit digit is 4 → Divisible by 2, but not divisible by 5.

⇒ For 130: The unit digit is 0 → Divisible by both 2 and 5.

⇒ For 135: The unit digit is 5 → Divisible by 5, but not divisible by 2.

A number is divisible by 4 if the value formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a multiple of 8.

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions evaluates to either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: As stated by French President Emmanuel Macron on 9 June 2025, how many countries had ratified the High Seas Treaty by that date?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**49**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• French President **Emmanuel Macron** announced on **9 June 2025**, during the lead-up to the **UN Ocean Conference** in **Nice**, that **49 countries** had ratified the **High Seas Treaty**.

• The treaty, formally known as the **BBNJ Treaty** (Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction), requires **60 ratifications** to officially enter into force.

• This announcement was a significant milestone in the global effort to protect international waters, which cover nearly **two-thirds** of the global ocean surface. ***Hence, the correct answer is 49.***

• The **High Seas Treaty** was adopted by the **United Nations** on **19 June 2023**, following nearly two decades of negotiations to establish a legal framework for the conservation of marine life in international waters.

• The treaty aims to establish **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)** in the high seas, which are areas beyond the **Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ)** of individual nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **The BBNJ Agreement:**

• It is an international agreement under the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)**.

• It focuses on four main pillars: **Marine Genetic Resources (MGRs)**, Area-based management tools including **Marine Protected Areas**, **Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs)**, and Capacity building and the transfer of marine technology.

• The treaty is vital for achieving the **"30x30" goal**, a target set under the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework** to protect **30%** of the world’s land and oceans by the **year 2030**.

• **Ratification Process:**

• For an international treaty to become legally binding, a country must first **sign** it and then **ratify** it through its domestic legislative process.

• The **60-country threshold** is the designated number required to trigger the treaty's activation **120 days** after the 60th instrument of ratification is deposited.

• President **Emmanuel Macron** has been a vocal advocate for the treaty, launching the **High Ambition Coalition** on BBNJ at the **One Ocean Summit** in **Brest, France**, in **February 2022**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **The High Seas:**

• These are areas of the ocean that do not belong to any state's jurisdiction. They represent **95%** of the Earth's habitat by volume but are among the least protected regions on the planet.

• Before this treaty, only about **1%** of the high seas were under any form of management or protection.

• The **2025 UN Ocean Conference** in **Nice, France**, co-hosted by **France** and **Costa Rica**, served as a major platform for accelerating the ratification count toward the **60-nation** target.

• **Marine Genetic Resources:** One of the most debated aspects of the treaty involves the equitable sharing of benefits derived from **genetic material** of marine plants and animals found in the deep sea.

questions.question: The Environment Audit Rules, 2025, are aligned with which national reform agenda in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ease of Doing Business**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Environment (Audit) Rules, 2025**, have been formulated by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to streamline the process of environmental compliance for industries in **India**.
 
• These rules are a significant step toward the national reform agenda of **Ease of Doing Business**, as they aim to reduce the regulatory burden on project proponents by simplifying reporting mechanisms.
 
• The primary objective is to replace the traditional "command and control" inspection regime with a more transparent, **self-regulatory**, and **third-party verification** system.
 
• Under these rules, industries are required to conduct regular audits to ensure they are meeting the standards set during their **Environmental Clearance (EC)** process.
 
• The alignment with **Ease of Doing Business** is evident as the rules promote **predictability**, **transparency**, and **efficiency** in environmental governance, which are critical for attracting **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**:
 
 
• The **Environment (Audit) Rules, 2025**, are framed under the powers conferred by the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, which was enacted following the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy** of **1984**.
 
• This umbrella legislation provides the **Central Government** with the authority to protect and improve environmental quality and control pollution.
 
 
 
• **Accreditation of Auditors**:
 
 
• The rules mandate that environmental audits must be carried out by **accredited environmental auditors** or agencies recognized by the **Quality Council of India (QCI)** or the **National Accreditation Board for Education and Training (NABET)**.
 
• This ensures that the data provided to the **government** is accurate, professional, and scientifically sound.
 
 
 
• **PARIVESH Portal**:
 
 
• The **Environment Audit** reports are integrated into the **PARIVESH** (Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub) portal.
 
• This **digital India** initiative serves as a **single-window** system for all environmental, forest, wildlife, and CRZ clearances, further enhancing the **Ease of Doing Business**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Categorization and Frequency**:
 
 
• Industries are often categorized into **Red**, **Orange**, and **Green** categories based on their **Pollution Index (PI)**. The **2025 Rules** specify different audit frequencies based on these categories to optimize resources.
 
• High-pollution (**Red**) industries are subject to more frequent and rigorous environmental audits compared to less polluting ones.
 
 
 
• **Compliance and Penalties**:
 
 
• The rules emphasize **compliance** with the conditions stipulated in the **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)**.
 
• Non-compliance or submission of fraudulent audit reports can lead to heavy **penalties**, **cancellation of clearances**, or legal action under **Section 15** of the **Environment (Protection) Act**, which includes **imprisonment** for up to **5 years** or a fine up to **1 lakh rupees**, or both.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)**:
 
 
• While focusing on **Ease of Doing Business**, the rules also align with **India's** commitment to **Sustainable Development Goals**, specifically **SDG 12** (Responsible Consumption and Production) and **SDG 13** (Climate Action).
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct Act, set to be replaced by the Indian Ports Bill, 2025, passed by the Upper House of Parliament on 18 August 2025?

• This new legislation is designed to replace the **Indian Ports Act of 1908**, which had been the primary law regulating ports in India for over **117 years**.
 
• The primary objective of the **2025 Bill** is to repeal the archaic colonial-era **1908 Act** and provide a contemporary regulatory framework that addresses the current needs of the **maritime sector**, including safety, security, and administrative efficiency.
 
• The bill focuses on the holistic development of **non-major ports** (also known as minor ports) and ensures that their management is aligned with international maritime standards and **global best practices**.
 
• It empowers the **Maritime State Development Council (MSDC)** to act as an apex advisory body to ensure integrated planning and development of the entire **port sector** across the country's vast coastline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indian Ports Act, 1908:**
 
 
• Enacted during the **British colonial period**, this act provided for the administration of ports and the imposition of **port-dues**.
 
• It lacked comprehensive provisions for **environmental protection**, modern security protocols, and the structured development of **private sector participation** in port operations.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Indian Ports Bill, 2025:**
 
 
• **Safety and Security:** The bill incorporates the **International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code**, ensuring that Indian ports meet global security requirements to prevent **maritime terrorism** and smuggling.
 
• **Pollution Control:** It introduces stringent measures for the **prevention of marine pollution**, mandating ports to have adequate facilities for the reception of **ship-generated waste** and oil residues.
 
• **Digitalization:** The legislation promotes the use of the **National Logistics Portal-Marine** to facilitate **Ease of Doing Business** by automating port clearances and documentation.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Ports in India:**
 
 
• **Major Ports:** Currently, India has **12 Major Ports** that are governed by the **Major Port Authorities Act, 2021**, and fall under the jurisdiction of the **Central Government**.
 
• **Non-Major Ports:** There are over **200 Non-Major Ports** distributed across the maritime states and Union Territories, which are generally managed by the **State Governments** or **Maritime Boards**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Maritime State Development Council (MSDC):** This council is a permanent body created to foster consultation between the **Union Government** and **State Governments**. It plays a critical role in preventing the duplication of port infrastructure and optimizing the use of **India's 7,517 km coastline**.
 
• **Economic Significance:** Approximately **95% by volume** and **70% by value** of India's external trade is handled through **maritime transport**, making the replacement of the **1908 Act** vital for achieving the target of a **5 trillion-dollar economy**.
 
• **Adjudication:** The **2025 Bill** provides for an **Adjudicatory Authority** to resolve disputes between ports and users, ensuring a transparent and time-bound grievance redressal mechanism.
</ul
